 One Comment 
 Cameron Kiszla 
 October 27, 2026 
 A former Los Angeles Dodgers pitcher could be the key piece in the Milwaukee Brewers’ pursuit of their first ever World Series title and earn his third ring in the process.
 Pitcher Dustin May already has two rings from his time with the Los Angeles Dodgers, and now, he could be the starting pitcher who brings home a ring for the Brewers.
 What World Series titles does Dustin May already have?
 May won his first World Series in 2020 as a young pitcher for the Dodgers.
 He missed the entirety of the 2024 season due to elbow surgery and a torn esophagus, though he returned for 2025.
 View this post on Instagram A post shared by Dodgers Nation (@dodgersnation) 
 That year, he was dealt to the Boston Red Sox, though he still got a ring for his contributions after the Dodgers’ dramatic Game 7 victory over the Toronto Blue Jays.
 So while May is ineligible for a personal three-peat, he still can win the third ring of his career, perhaps as soon as Tuesday night.
 Dustin May’s chance to make history
 May is getting the start for the Brewers Tuesday night , providing him a chance to get the clinching win.
 The Brewers have a 3-0 lead against the Tampa Bay Rays, and Monday night’s game was a 10-1 thrashing.
 May 17, 2023; Los Angeles, California, USA; Los Angeles Dodgers starting pitcher Dustin May (85) throws against the Minnesota Twins during the first inning at Dodger Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Gary A. Vasquez-USA TODAY Sports It’s a remarkable opportunity after that 2024 season could have marked the end of May’s career.
 “For me, honestly, I’m just going to go and do exactly what I can in the moment and live pitch by pitch … For everything that I’ve been through the last six years, for me, it means more to be here in this moment today knowing two years ago, looking back where I was, I wasn’t really sure if I was ever going to play again,” May said to MLB Network . “So being able to be here in this moment, it truly means the world to me. I couldn’t attribute anything more to the Lord and my wife for letting me be here in this moment, to be here today.”
 Oct 6, 2026; San Diego, California, USA; Milwaukee Brewers pitcher Dustin May (21) pitches during the first inning against the San Diego Padres in game three of the NLDS for the 2026 MLB Playoffs at Petco Park. Mandatory Credit: David Frerker-Imagn Images It’s been a long road back to the World Series for May, but he’s getting another shot.
 Do you think Dustin May will be able to close out the World Series Tuesday night?
